#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
# never-shipped commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor; do
  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
done
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --print-memmap ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --print-memmap:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
# The ROI pipeline-trace knobs are user-facing: --kanata, with --objdump
# nested under it (it requires --kanata, like the pc pair under --trigger).
has '^  --kanata '    "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^    --objdump ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --objdump nested under --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column.
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
# it. (Checked as the '^  fixtures ' target line, not the bare word -- doctor's
# brief legitimately mentions checking fixtures are present.)
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$LH" && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
has '^  models '   "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$DLH" || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
DOC=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"
ok "doctor missing-artifact hint points at scripts/build_all.sh, not the removed command"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
# never-shipped commands (cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)

has '^list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"

has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"

has '^  --print-memmap ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --print-memmap:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"

# nested under it (it requires --kanata, like the pc pair under --trigger).

has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"

# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, profile, list, doctor) and never the third-party
# simulator name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff
# have moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
# never-shipped commands (cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^run '     "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^profile ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'profile':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^list '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor; do
  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
done
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --print-memmap ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --print-memmap:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
# The ROI pipeline-trace knobs are user-facing: --kanata, with --objdump
# nested under it (it requires --kanata, like the pc pair under --trigger).
has '^  --kanata '    "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^    --objdump ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --objdump nested under --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column.
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
# it. (Checked as the '^  fixtures ' target line, not the bare word -- doctor's
# brief legitimately mentions checking fixtures are present.)
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$LH" && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
has '^  models '   "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$DLH" || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
DOC=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"
ok "doctor missing-artifact hint points at scripts/build_all.sh, not the removed command"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# `andesim profile` LLM report contract (real QEMU + the hot-loop TCG plugin):
# each loop block carries a ready hybrid pc window,
# `measure: --pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>`, derived from the loop's
# enclosing function (one-shot pc triggers fire on the first hit, so the
# function span covers every iteration and needs no objdump step).
#
# profile is engine-synced, so the test ships a fake cycle-accurate engine
# (ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR) whose --describe pins vlen=512 and whose
# --print-qemu-config names andes-ax45mpv -- the same cfg staging a real
# vsim engine gets, without needing one built. The plugin path is NOT
# overridable from the CLI: the run proves the bundled
# qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so resolution end to end.
#
# Builds a tiny single-ret RVV kernel (vplat runtime), profiles it, and
# checks the measure line against the toolchain's own nm/objdump as the
# oracle.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null || true
QEMU_BIN="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
GCC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"
OBJDUMP="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

[ -x "$QEMU_BIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: external qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"; exit 0; }
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so" ] || { echo "SKIP: hotloops plugin not built (make -C qemu_plugin)"; exit 0; }
[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "SKIP: no riscv toolchain"; exit 0; }
[ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime" ] || { echo "SKIP: vplat runtime not built"; exit 0; }
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: build/andesim missing"; exit 1; }

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t hotloops-measure.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The fake engine profile derives its QEMU config from: vlen=512 via
# --describe, -cpu andes-ax45mpv via the staged --print-qemu-config.
mkdir -p "$TMP/engines"
cat >"$TMP/engines/v1" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:fake512","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":512,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
elif [ "$1" = "--print-qemu-config" ]; then
  printf '[global]\ndriver = "andes-ax45mpv-riscv-cpu"\nproperty = "vext_spec"\nvalue = "v1.0"\n'
fi
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/engines/v1"

cat > "$TMP/vadd.c" <<'EOF'
#include <stdint.h>
#include <riscv_vector.h>
static int32_t a[64], b[64];
__attribute__((noinline)) static void vadd_kernel(void)
{
  for (int r = 0; r < 50; r++)
    for (int i = 0; i < 64;) {
      size_t vl = __riscv_vsetvl_e32m1((size_t) (64 - i));
      vint32m1_t va = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&a[i], vl);
      vint32m1_t vb = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&b[i], vl);
      __riscv_vse32_v_i32m1(&a[i], __riscv_vadd_vv_i32m1(va, vb, vl), vl);
      i += (int) vl;
    }
}
int main(void) { vadd_kernel(); return 0; }
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$ROOT/build/runtime" -specs=andesim.specs \
  "$TMP/vadd.c" -o "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: fixture build failed"; exit 1; }

REPORT=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/engines" "$BIN" profile \
           --min-iters 10 "$TMP/vadd.elf" 2>/dev/null)

echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "\[hottest\]" \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no hottest loop reported"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }

MEASURE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure:")
[ -n "$MEASURE" ] \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure: line in the report"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }

GOT_S=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
GOT_E=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')

# Oracle: the kernel's entry from nm; its return = the function's last
# instruction (single-epilogue at -O1; objdump flavors disagree on the
# `ret` vs `c.jr ra` spelling, so match by position, not mnemonic).
WANT_S=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$NM" "$TMP/vadd.elf" | awk '$3=="vadd_kernel"{print $1; exit}')")
WANT_E=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  | sed -n '/<vadd_kernel>:/,/^$/p' | grep -E '^[ ]+[0-9a-f]+:' \
  | tail -1 | awk '{sub(":","",$1); print $1}')")

if [ "$GOT_S" != "$WANT_S" ] || [ "$GOT_E" != "$WANT_E" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: window $GOT_S..$GOT_E, want $WANT_S..$WANT_E"
  echo "$MEASURE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "PASS[hotloops_measure]: measure = $GOT_S .. $GOT_E (all of vadd_kernel), via 'andesim profile' + bundled plugin"

file.content:
# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so  -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotloops.so        -- hot inner-loop detector (developer profiling tool)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotloops.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

# hotloops is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not HYBRID_INCLUDE.
libhotloops.so: hotloops.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotloops.c $(LIBS)

clean:
	rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotloops.so

# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so  -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotloops.so        -- hot inner-loop detector (developer profiling tool)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotloops.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

# hotloops is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not HYBRID_INCLUDE.
libhotloops.so: hotloops.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotloops.c $(LIBS)

clean:
	rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotloops.so

1	# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector
2	
3	Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
4	translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
5	loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
6	count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
7	present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
8	
9	Two parts ship together:
10	
11	- `qemu_plugin/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
12	- `build/hotloops` - C++ tool (source `driver/hotloops.cpp`) that runs the
13	  plugin and formats output.
14	
15	## Usage
16	
17	```
18	build/hotloops [options] <elf>
19	```
20	
21	The tool launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
22	machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
23	`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
24	for other targets.
25	
26	### Options
27	
28	| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
29	|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
30	| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
31	| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
32	| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
33	| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
34	| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
35	| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
36	| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
37	| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
38	| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
39	| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
40	| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
41	| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
42	| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
43	| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
44	| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
45	| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
46	| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
47	| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |
48	
49	### Build prerequisites
50	
51	The plugin lives in `qemu_plugin/`. Build once:
52	
53	```
54	make -C qemu_plugin
55	```
56	
57	It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
58	themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
59	to be rebuilt.
60	
61	## How it detects a loop
62	
63	For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
64	instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
65	remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
66	The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
67	iterations.
68	
69	This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
70	goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
71	semantics.
72	
73	Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
74	that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
75	on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.
76	
77	## Output modes
78	
79	Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:
80	
81	1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
82	2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
83	3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).
84	
85	### LLM report (default)
86	
87	The tool emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
88	reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
89	first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.
90	
91	Layout:
92	
93	- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
94	  `rvv_filter`.
95	- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
96	  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
97	  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
98	- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
99	  - `iters` and `pc_range` (`0xstart .. 0xend  (size: N B)`).
100	  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff`).
101	  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
102	    tail map to different lines).
103	  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
104	    in DWARF.
105	  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
106	    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
107	  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
108	    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
109	    same-function nesting.
110	  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
111	    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
112	    show as `(indirect)`.
113	
114	The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
115	no LLM call is made by the tool itself.
116	
117	Limitations:
118	
119	- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
120	  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
121	  `calls:` to bridge.
122	- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
123	  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
124	  fall back to just `file:line`.
125	- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
126	  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
127	  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.
128	
129	### Table mode (`--no-llm`)
130	
131	Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:
132	
133	```
134	# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
135	iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
136	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
137	<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
138	...
139	```
140	
141	Columns:
142	
143	- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
144	- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
145	- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
146	- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
147	                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
148	                FUNC symbol.
149	- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
150	                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
151	                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
152	                info and `--no-source` is not set.
153	
154	### Raw mode (`--raw`)
155	
156	Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
157	plugin output:
158	
159	```
160	hotloops: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
161	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
162	0x..., 0x..., <n>
163	...
164	```
165	
166	Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.
167	
168	## Example
169	
170	A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:
171	
172	```c
173	/* hotloops_demo.c - baremetal entry */
174	#include <stdint.h>
175	
176	__attribute__((noinline))
177	static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
178	    int s = 0;
179	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
180	    return s;
181	}
182	
183	void main(void) {
184	    static int a[64], b[64];
185	    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
186	    long total = 0;
187	    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
188	        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
189	    (void)total;
190	}
191	```
192	
193	Build for AE350 with the Andes RISC-V toolchain (or any baremetal
194	RVV-capable toolchain), then run:
195	
196	```
197	$ build/hotloops --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
198	```
199	
200	LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:
201	
202	```markdown
203	# Hotloops Report
204	target:           hotloops_demo.elf
205	total_iters:      32000
206	reported_loops:   1
207	min_iters:        100
208	rvv_filter:       on
209	
210	## TL;DR
211	Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
212	total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
213	(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.
214	
215	## Loops
216	
217	### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
218	iters:        31500
219	pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
220	function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
221	source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
222	code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
223	rvv:          yes (4 insns)
224	rvv_insns:
225	  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
226	  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
227	  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
228	  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
229	parent:       -
230	children:     []
231	calls:        []
232	```
233	
234	Reading the report:
235	
236	- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
237	  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
238	- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
239	  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
240	  of branching back).
241	- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
242	  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
243	  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
244	  loops too).
245	
246	For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:
247	
248	```
249	$ build/hotloops --raw build/hotloops_demo.elf | head
250	hotloops: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
251	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
252	0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
253	```
254	
255	## Tips
256	
257	- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
258	  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
259	  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
260	- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
261	  to see the full distribution.
262	- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
263	  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
264	  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
265	- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
266	  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
267	  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
268	- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.
269

RVV-capable toolchain), then run:

```
$ build/hotloops --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
```

```markdown

target:           hotloops_demo.elf
total_iters:      32000
reported_loops:   1
min_iters:        100
rvv_filter:       on

## TL;DR
Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.

## Loops

### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
iters:        31500
pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
rvv:          yes (4 insns)
rvv_insns:
  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
parent:       -
children:     []
calls:        []

- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
  of branching back).
- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
  loops too).

For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:

```
$ build/hotloops --raw build/hotloops_demo.elf | head
hotloops: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
```

## Tips

- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
  to see the full distribution.
- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.

# andesim profile - hot inner-loop detector

Finds the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in QEMU. For each detected loop you get the
loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, the iteration count, and a ready
`measure: --pc-start .. --pc-end ..` window you can paste into a hybrid
run. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `qemu_plugin/hotIterationLoop.c` - QEMU TCG plugin
  (`libhotIterationLoop.so`) that records edges.
- `andesim profile` - the driver command that picks the engine, launches
  QEMU with the plugin, and formats the report.

## Usage

```
./andesim profile [--engine <id>] [options] <elf> [-- <extra qemu args>]
```

profile is engine-synced, exactly like hybrid: it picks a cycle-accurate
engine (`--engine <id>`, or the sole installed one) and derives the QEMU
launch from it -- the `-cpu` model from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`
probe, `vlen` from its `--describe`, and the probe's config staged as
`-readconfig`. So the profile sees the same ISA the engine will measure:
a different `vlen` changes `vsetvl` trip counts, which changes the loop
ranking itself.

If the engine does not answer `--print-qemu-config`, profile warns and
falls back to the family-default `-cpu` (the report may then not match
the engine's ISA).

### Options

| Flag                | Default   | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--engine <id>`     | sole one  | The engine whose QEMU config to profile on (`./andesim list engines`). |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50        | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1         | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--optimize-rvv`    | on        | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
| `--no-optimize-rvv` | -         | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
| `--llm`             | on        | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
| `--no-llm`          | -         | Emit the plain human-readable table instead.                   |
| `--no-source`       | off       | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
| `--objdump <bin>`   | auto      | Override objdump (default: `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`'s riscv objdump). |
| `--addr2line <bin>` | auto      | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
| `--raw`             | off       | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
| `--mem-size <spec>` | QEMU dflt | Guest RAM, forwarded as QEMU `-m`.                             |
| `--dry-run`         | off       | Print the exact QEMU command and exit, running nothing.        |
| `-- <args...>`      | -         | Everything after `--` is forwarded verbatim to QEMU.           |

The old standalone `build/hotloops` tool and its QEMU-shape flags
(`--arch`, `--qemu`, `--plugin`, `--machine`, `--cpu`, `--qemu-config`,
`--cwd`, `--qemu-arg`) are gone: the engine and `config.env` decide the
QEMU shape now, and extra QEMU args ride the `--` passthrough.

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `qemu_plugin/`. Build once:

```
make -C qemu_plugin
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotIterationLoop.c`. The QEMU
binaries themselves do **not** need to be rebuilt.

## How it detects a loop

For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
iterations.

This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
semantics.

Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.

## Output modes

Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:

1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).

### LLM report (default)

The command emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.

Layout:

- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
  `rvv_filter`.
- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
  - `iters`.
  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff` at the loop's header and tail).
  - `measure` - a ready `--pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>` pair
    covering the loop's whole enclosing function (entry -> ret). Paste it
    straight into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`.
  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
    tail map to different lines).
  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
    in DWARF.
  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
    same-function nesting.
  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
    show as `(indirect)`.

The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
no LLM call is made by the command itself.

Limitations:

- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
  `calls:` to bridge.
- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
  fall back to just `file:line`.
- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.

### Table mode (`--no-llm`)

Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:

```
# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
...
```

Columns:

- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
                FUNC symbol.
- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to

# andesim profile - hot inner-loop detector

Finds the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in QEMU. For each detected loop you get the
loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, the iteration count, and a ready
`measure: --pc-start .. --pc-end ..` window you can paste into a hybrid
run. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `qemu_plugin/hotIterationLoop.c` - QEMU TCG plugin
  (`libhotIterationLoop.so`) that records edges.
- `andesim profile` - the driver command that picks the engine, launches
  QEMU with the plugin, and formats the report.

## Usage

```
./andesim profile [--engine <id>] [options] <elf> [-- <extra qemu args>]
```

profile is engine-synced, exactly like hybrid: it picks a cycle-accurate
engine (`--engine <id>`, or the sole installed one) and derives the QEMU
launch from it -- the `-cpu` model from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`
probe, `vlen` from its `--describe`, and the probe's config staged as
`-readconfig`. So the profile sees the same ISA the engine will measure:
a different `vlen` changes `vsetvl` trip counts, which changes the loop
ranking itself.

If the engine does not answer `--print-qemu-config`, profile warns and
falls back to the family-default `-cpu` (the report may then not match
the engine's ISA).

### Options

| Flag                | Default   | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--engine <id>`     | sole one  | The engine whose QEMU config to profile on (`./andesim list engines`). |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50        | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1         | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--optimize-rvv`    | on        | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
| `--no-optimize-rvv` | -         | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
| `--llm`             | on        | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
| `--no-llm`          | -         | Emit the plain human-readable table instead.                   |
| `--no-source`       | off       | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
| `--objdump <bin>`   | auto      | Override objdump (default: `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`'s riscv objdump). |
| `--addr2line <bin>` | auto      | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
| `--raw`             | off       | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
| `--mem-size <spec>` | QEMU dflt | Guest RAM, forwarded as QEMU `-m`.                             |
| `--dry-run`         | off       | Print the exact QEMU command and exit, running nothing.        |
| `-- <args...>`      | -         | Everything after `--` is forwarded verbatim to QEMU.           |

The old standalone `build/hotloops` tool and its QEMU-shape flags
(`--arch`, `--qemu`, `--plugin`, `--machine`, `--cpu`, `--qemu-config`,
`--cwd`, `--qemu-arg`) are gone: the engine and `config.env` decide the
QEMU shape now, and extra QEMU args ride the `--` passthrough.

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `qemu_plugin/`. Build once:

```
make -C qemu_plugin
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotIterationLoop.c`. The QEMU
binaries themselves do **not** need to be rebuilt.

## How it detects a loop

For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
iterations.

This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
semantics.

Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.

## Output modes

Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:

1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).

### LLM report (default)

The command emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.

Layout:

- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
  `rvv_filter`.
- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
  - `iters`.
  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff` at the loop's header and tail).
  - `measure` - a ready `--pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>` pair
    covering the loop's whole enclosing function (entry -> ret). Paste it
    straight into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`.
  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
    tail map to different lines).
  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
    in DWARF.
  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.

...

...
```

- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.

### Table mode (`--no-llm`)

Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:

```
# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
...
```

Columns:

- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
                FUNC symbol.
- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
                info and `--no-source` is not set.

### Raw mode (`--raw`)

Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
plugin output:

```
hotIterationLoop: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x..., 0x..., <n>
...
```

Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.

## Example

A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:

```c
/* profile_demo.c - baremetal entry */
#include <stdint.h>

__attribute__((noinline))
static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
    int s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
    return s;
}

void main(void) {
    static int a[64], b[64];
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
    long total = 0;
    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
    (void)total;
}
```

Build it against the vplat runtime (USER_GUIDE section 4), then run:

```
$ ./andesim profile --min-iters 100 --limit 5 profile_demo.elf
```

LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:

```markdown
# HotIterationLoop Report
target:           profile_demo.elf
total_iters:      32000
reported_loops:   1
min_iters:        100
rvv_filter:       on

## TL;DR
Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (profile_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.

## Loops

### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
iters:        31500
function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
measure:      --pc-start 0x80000200 --pc-end 0x80000230  (all of dot_rvv: entry -> ret)
source:       profile_demo.c:6
code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
rvv:          yes (4 insns)
rvv_insns:
  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
parent:       -
children:     []
calls:        []
```

Reading the report:

- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
- The `measure:` line is the handoff to hybrid: run
  `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --pc-start 0x80000200
  --pc-end 0x80000230 profile_demo.elf` to get the cycle figure for all
  of `dot_rvv` on the same engine the profile ran against.
- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
  of branching back).
- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
  loops too).

For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:

```
$ ./andesim profile --raw profile_demo.elf | head
hotIterationLoop: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
start_pc, end_pc, iterations
0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
```

## Tips

- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
  to see the full distribution.
- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.
- `--dry-run` shows the exact QEMU command (including the staged
  `-readconfig` and the engine-derived `-cpu`) without running anything.

file.content:
## 1. What andesim is

andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:

| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |

`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).

One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.

---

## 2. Check your installation

```sh
./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
./andesim list models     # the three models
./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
```

`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.

`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:

```
ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
```

`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.

Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
the long version.

---

## 3. First runs

## 6. The `profile` command -- find your ROI first

When you do not yet know WHERE the hot region is, run `profile` before
`run --mode hybrid`:

```sh
./andesim profile [--engine <id>] my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the whole ELF under QEMU with a loop-detector plugin
(`libhotIterationLoop.so`) and prints a Markdown report of the hottest
loops. Each loop block ends with a ready window:

```
measure:      --pc-start 0x10007c --pc-end 0x1000c2  (all of vadd_kernel: entry -> ret)
```

Paste that pair into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` to
measure exactly that function on the cycle engine.

profile picks its engine the same way hybrid does (`--engine <id>`, or
the sole installed cycle-accurate engine) and launches QEMU with THAT
engine's configuration -- the same `-cpu`/`-readconfig` sync a hybrid
fast leg gets. So the loop ranking reflects the ISA (including VLEN) of
the engine you will measure on.

Useful knobs: `--min-iters <N>` drops cold loops, `--limit <N>` caps the
report, `--no-optimize-rvv` also shows scalar loops (the default reports
RVV-containing loops only), `--no-llm` prints a plain table, `--dry-run`
previews the QEMU command. Full reference: `docs/profile.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# HVM transport F3 (ROADMAP_hvm): the driver arms the HVM content transport
# from the accurate engine's descriptor, exactly like ILM/DLM --
#   fast leg   : plugin args gain ",hvm_size=<bytes>" (sidecar drain)
#   accurate leg: argv gains "--hvm <state_in>.hvm"   (backdoor load)
# and an engine describing hvm_size=0 must arm NEITHER. Asserted through
# `--dry-run`, which prints the exact argvs without running engines.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"     # fail/ok + vsim_bin_dir
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"   # hybrid_describe_int

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
PREMIUM="$BINDIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
if [ ! -x "$PREMIUM" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: no sim_ax45mpv_premium under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
  exit 0
fi

# The engine's own advertised size is the wiring's source of truth.
HVM_SIZE=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size "$PREMIUM")
[ -n "$HVM_SIZE" ] && [ "$HVM_SIZE" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "premium --describe lacks a non-zero hvm_size (vsim F1 regression?)"

out=$(timeout 60 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
      --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE" \
  || fail "fast-leg plugin args lack hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
  || fail "accurate-leg argv lacks --hvm <state>.hvm: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'ilm_size=' \
  || fail "LM wiring regressed (no ilm_size= in plugin args): $out"
ok "premium: plugin hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE + accurate-leg --hvm armed"

# Negative: an engine that describes hvm_size=0 (ax46: config has HVM, wrapper
# has no backdoor) must arm neither side.
AX46="$BINDIR/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 60 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
        --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax46mpv_advanced "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "ax46 hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hvm_size=' \
    && fail "ax46 (hvm_size 0) must not arm the plugin hvm drain: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
    && fail "ax46 (hvm_size 0) must not get --hvm: $out"
  ok "ax46: hvm transport stays off (describe hvm_size=0)"
else
  ok "SKIP ax46 negative: no sim_ax46mpv_advanced under $BINDIR"
fi

echo "PASS[andes_sim_hvm_wiring]"

Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |

| `dlm_size` | number          | no       | Hart-0 DLM size in BYTES (0 / omit = none). |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, profile, list, doctor) and never the third-party
# simulator name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff
# have moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
# never-shipped commands (cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^run '     "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^profile ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'profile':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^list '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run profile list doctor; do
  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
done
for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --print-memmap ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --print-memmap:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
# The ROI pipeline-trace knobs are user-facing: --kanata, with --objdump
# nested under it (it requires --kanata, like the pc pair under --trigger).
has '^  --kanata '    "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^    --objdump ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --objdump nested under --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"

for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do

[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'

LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)

no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column.
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
